problem: Image-goal navigation policies must infer the target pose from a goal image alone, and end-to-end policies without explicit geometric reasoning struggle to find the goal pose accurately and efficiently.
motivation: A robot needs to reach the exact pose from which a target image was taken. The paper's premise is that estimating the geometric relation (viewpoint) between the current and target views gives the policy a useful signal for choosing actions.
key_idea: Add an auxiliary viewpoint estimation module that predicts the geometric relation between the current view and the goal image, and feed that estimate to the navigation policy.
insight: The abstract reports that giving the agent the ability to estimate geometric information improves success and time efficiency by a large margin. The authors also run experiments on how this estimation ability affects navigation. Only the abstract was available, so no specific ablation results can be cited.
method: Viewpoint estimation: estimates the geometric information (relative pose) between the target pose and the robot's current pose from the images.
Navigation policy: uses the estimated geometric information to predict actions that reach the target pose.

setting.training_data: Gibson dataset in Habitat (details not given in abstract)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (probably with depth) plus goal image
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (not specified in abstract)

numbers_note: abstract only; no numeric results given
results: The abstract states that adding geometric information estimation makes the agent find the target pose much more successfully and time-efficiently on Habitat with Gibson. No numbers or baselines are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the evaluation details are unknown.
Evaluated only in simulation (Habitat/Gibson) according to the abstract.
